key_symbols.name: attachCmd
key_symbols.role: reads operator terminal size via term.GetSize and calls Engine.AttachArgv before exec'ing tmux

key_symbols.name: Engine.AttachArgv
key_symbols.role: builds the told-box attach pre-flight (pins, readbacks, layout plan) and chains select-layout onto attach-session, degrading to bare attach on any failure

key_symbols.name: chainedAttachArgv
key_symbols.role: composes the single tmux argv 'attach-session ; select-layout' so tmux resizes to the client before the layout string is applied

key_symbols.name: Engine.liveBoxLocked
key_symbols.role: queries tmux's live window size (display-message), falling back to configured cfg.Width/Height on failure

key_symbols.name: Engine.pinGeometryOptionsLocked
key_symbols.role: pins session 'status off' and 'window-size latest' so tmux tracks the attaching client's size

key_symbols.name: Engine.readWindowSizeLatestLocked / readStatusRowsLocked
key_symbols.role: read back effective pin values and suppress the chained layout if the pins didn't actually take

key_symbols.name: Engine.planLayout
key_symbols.role: pure function mapping a told render.Box + strand table to a tmux layout string; never queries geometry itself

key_symbols.name: Engine.applyLayoutLocked
key_symbols.role: non-attach reconciliation: fetches fresh liveBoxLocked box, plans layout, applies via select-layout/select-pane

key_symbols.name: Engine.reconcileApplyPersistLocked
key_symbols.role: shared tail every mutating verb runs: kill dead panes, re-list live, applyLayoutLocked, persist state

key_symbols.name: Geometry
key_symbols.role: struct of identity/path fields reed is told at construction; carries no width/height, so no geometry is persisted in reed.json

summary: Reed never persists a width/height in reed.json; geometry is always recomputed fresh from one of two live sources rather than diffed against a stored value. For an already-attached session, tmux's own 'window-size latest' pin (set by pinGeometryOptionsLocked) auto-tracks the client's terminal, and reed only re-applies a layout lazily on the next mutating CLI verb (add/remove/resume/up), each of which ends in reconcileApplyPersistLocked -> applyLayoutLocked -> a fresh liveBoxLocked() tmux query -> planLayout -> select-layout/select-pane. For re-attach, reedcli's attachCmd reads the operator's own terminal size via golang.org/x/term's GetSize and hands cols/rows straight to Engine.AttachArgv, which plans a layout against that told box (never liveBoxLocked, since the live window is still the stale pre-attach size at argv-build time) and chains 'select-layout' onto 'attach-session' in one tmux argv so tmux has already resized the window to the client before the layout string is applied, avoiding tmux's own silent proportional-rescale behavior. There is no explicit code-level comparison of old-vs-new geometry; the 'reconciliation' is really tmux's own layout application against whichever box (live-query or client-told) was most recently supplied, with reed's guards (option-pin readbacks, pane-count/anyPlacedStrand checks) only deciding whether to attempt a chained layout at all, always degrading to a bare, unlayouted attach on any doubt.
open_questions: Whether any resize while attached ever proactively triggers a reed op (versus purely lazy re-layout on the next CLI invocation) was not found in reedengine/reedcli; no SIGWINCH or push-based resize handler exists in these two packages.
